note.text: The simple past can tell a completed past sequence. The past perfect uses had + past participle to look back from a later past point. It helps show an earlier event or situation relevant at that point. Do not use had plus the simple-past form when the participle differs. Past perfect is not required for every earlier event if order is already clear; use it to make the intended perspective clear rather than marking ordinary chronological narration wrong.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to show the order of past events with simple past and had plus a participle. Builds on: simple past and the overview of perfect forms. Leads to: clear chronology in narratives and reports.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: The simple past can tell a completed past sequence. The past perfect uses had + past participle to look back from a later past point. It helps show an earlier event or situation relevant at that point. Do not use had plus the simple-past form when the participle differs. Past perfect is not required for every earlier event if order is already clear; use it to make the intended perspective clear rather than marking ordinary chronological narration wrong.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: When Ayuk arrived, Bih had {participle('write')} the note. Writing came before the later arrival. Compare Bih {past('write')} the note and then Ayuk arrived, which directly narrates the sequence. Had written supplies the look-back relationship; had wrote does not give the standard form.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Choose the later past reference point, identify the earlier event and select a participle. Keep the same event order when rewriting. A sequence word such as before can already clarify order, so context should determine whether past perfect is needed or simply useful.

cards.idea: Distinguish the ideas used in this lesson.
example: simple-past sequence: completed events narrated in their stated order.
past perfect: had plus a past participle looking back from a past point.
later reference point: the past event from which an earlier situation is viewed.
chronological signal: wording clarifying the order of events.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: Bih wrote the note and then Ayuk arrived.
Bih had {participle('write')} the note before the later arrival.
Ayuk’s arrival is the later point in when he arrived, Bih had written.
Then and before can help show the sequence.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: A past narrative cannot use more than one simple-past verb. Correction: Simple past can narrate a chronological sequence.
Had wrote is the standard perfect form of write. Correction: Had takes the participle written.
The later reference point must always occur in the future. Correction: Both events can be past; the reference point is later within that past.
Every earlier action must use past perfect even when the order is already clear. Correction: Context and intended perspective determine the tense choice.
